messages:
pagerduty-bot: [PAGER] high-severity: GPU nodepool exhausted — queue length for gpu-jobs > 18k, 60m growth, autoscaler failing to add nodes :rotating_light:
Alex (oncall): ack, paged and joining. observed 5xx spike on hosted inference, kat-client indicates token generation timeouts.
Mira (sre): seeing cluster-autoscaler logs showing errors adding nodes: 
```
Failed to create instance: AutoScalingGroup capacity limits reached for nodegroup-gpu-prod (Desired 20, Max 20)
Error: LaunchTemplate version mismatch: launch template version 3 not found
```
Sam (infra): We recently rolled a launch template v4 to new nodegroups, but this nodegroup still pinned to v3. ASG max set to 20 (commit). looks like queue spike hit the committed pool limit.
Karim (ml-infra): queue growth from batched inference jobs — rate ~350rps. Fallbacks are queued until GPU nodes available. Customer-facing latencies >30s.
Julia (support): we have multiple customer escalations — two enterprise customers seeing timeouts. raising priority.
Alex (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) manual scale up ephemeral GPU ASG (if possible) 2) increase nodegroup max temporarily 3) drain low-priority pods to free GPU slots 4) enable cpu-fallback . who can run steps 1 and 2?
Sam (infra): I can run but need IAM permission; console attach failed earlier due to instance profile missing `ec2:RunInstances` on the launchtemplate role. hitting IAM deny when ASG tries to roll new instances. logs: `AccessDenied: You are not authorized to perform: ec2:RunInstances`
Mira (sre): that IAM deny explains some errors. while Sam sorts IAM, we can try manual provisioning of a warm fleet in a different ASG that uses a different instance profile — I can request override from infra-admin.
Karim (ml-infra): also, some pods are tainted/tolerations mismatched — scheduler won't place pods on the ephemeral nodes unless tolerations added. we can patch the gpu-job controller to toleration `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule`? that's not right. better: make ephemeral nodes with matching taints or remove taints temporarily.
Alex (oncall): steps executed: Sam to request IAM fix + bump max for nodegroup-gpu-prod to 30, Mira to create ephemeral ASG with working launch template, Karim patch controller for tolerations for ephemeral nodes, Julia coordinating customer comms. update every 5m.
Sam (infra): requesting IAM change now. pinging infra-admin @samuel-aws. also issuing ASG increase request: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name nodegroup-gpu-prod --max-size 30 --desired-capacity 25` (dry run blocked by IAM; will retry after grant).
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: `launch-template/v4 -> nodegroup-gpu-prod` queued — blocked by IAM.
Mira (sre): meanwhile I spun up a small pool of cpu fallback runners and started requeuing non-latency-critical jobs to CPU. this buys ~12k jobs cleared over last 10m. queue length down to ~6.5k but GPU-critical backlog remains 6.2k.
Karim (ml-infra): patch applied to gpu-job controller to add toleration for `ephemeral-gpu:true:NoSchedule` and created ephemeral ASG nodes with that taint. pods are now binding to some of them.
Sam (infra): IAM change approved by infra-admin (role EC2LaunchRole now has ec2:RunInstances), re-triggering ASG scale. autoscaler log after retry: 
```
ScalingActivity: Launching a new EC2 instance: i-0abc1234
Successfully launched 5 instances
```
Mira (sre): cluster-autoscaler still logs a warning: `failed to update nodegroup status: launch template version mismatch for nodegroup-gpu-prod (expected 4 actual 3)`. I've patched the nodegroup to point at LT v4. will attempt a rolling update.
Alex (oncall): rolling update might evict pods; schedule_tmaintenance? how long estimate?
Mira (sre): ~6-8m for rolling update to replace instances. doing surge replacement at 2 at a time.
Julia (support): customer update drafted: "We are actively mitigating an infrastructure capacity issue affecting GPU inference jobs. Some requests may see increased latency; we will post updates every 15 minutes." send after next checkpoint.
Karim (ml-infra): after ephemeral nodes + new instances, GPU job starts scheduling again. metrics: GPU utilization ~85% on new nodes, backlog down to ~2.1k. latency for affected customers trending down to 3-5s for new requests.
Alex (oncall): great. next actions: 1) keep ASG max bumped until postmortem 2) reconcile launchtemplate versions across nodegroups 3) fix IAM policy to allow autoscaler/ASG rotations without manual intervention 4) add alert to warn when nodegroup max == requested desired for >5m.
Sam (infra): filing infra ticket to lower friction: attach autoscaler service role, add test on infra CI to validate LT versions. ticket: INFRA-895
Mira (sre): marking incident as "mitigated" but still monitoring. will leave channel open for 30m then handoff to ops-runbook.
Julia (support): informing affected customers per template and offering rollback to previous SLA window for critical customers.
Alex (oncall): thanks all. final state snapshot: queue from 18k -> 2.1k, latency for critical endpoints back to baseline, ASG max temporarily 30, IAM fix applied, launchtemplate normalized to v4. creating incident postmortem stub.
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Alex (oncall), severity downgraded to P2 and assigned to Mira (sre) for post-incident review.
Mira (sre): I'll run through root cause: combined factors: traffic surge + committed ASG capacity hit + launch template version drift + missing IAM perms preventing automated scaling. proposing follow-ups: automatic LT version sync job, limit-based alerting, and a staged increase policy for commit-burst events.
Alex (oncall): leaving final note: kudos to the team for quick modular mitigations (ephemeral pool + IAM fix + toleration patch). closing thread after postmortem draft. :heart:
